meta.about: A whole-node rewrite (`target` + `text`, no `find`) on a bullet with inline markup. `setText` used to write only the LONGEST text run and leave the others exactly as authored, so the old bolded/emphasised word survived next to the new wording with no separating space. Fixed by rewriting every run: the new text goes to the run least likely to carry unwanted styling, the rest are blanked.
meta.recorded-outcome: Asked to replace the Orama bullet ('Orama for the client-side vector store', italicised on 'Orama') with all-new wording, the model reached for `find` with the bullet's whole current text — which spans the italic span and the plain run, so `replaceText` refused it as "spans several separately-styled pieces of text". That refusal named no way to replace a WHOLE node, only "try a single word", so the model spent the rest of the conversation alternating between narrower `find` phrases and an ambiguous `target: "the bullets"` guess, and one turn it repeated the plain-bullet case ('A web-sized embedding model, quantized down') and gave up without even calling the tool. Reproducing `edit_text({target, text})` directly (bypassing the model) showed the deeper bug: the whole-node path silently 'succeeded', but left "A web-sized embedding model" untouched and appended the new text straight after it with no space, because `mainRunIndex` picked the LONGEST run to overwrite and left the rest alone.
meta.retargeted: the vector-search chapter became one slide of the runtime chapter, and then that slide lost its Orama bullet in a later rewrite. Now on "What is WebMCP?": its second bullet is `**Two APIs:** *Imperative* JavaScript, *declarative* HTML forms.`, which mixes bold, italic and plain runs, so a whole-line `find` still spans several and a revert of `setText` still leaves styled words behind. The slide has four bullets, not five, so the ambiguous `target: "the bullets"` refusal counts four. The word swapped for dogs is "Chrome", bold in bullet 3. The unscoped retry searches the whole deck, but only this slide is asserted. Bullet 2 is still node `.3`. Then "What is WebMCP?" became takeaway and detail pairs: the mixed node is takeaway detail 2 (`Imperative JavaScript, declarative HTML forms.`, node `.5`), and the turn-1 quote is that detail, not a whole bullet. With no bullets on the slide, turn 0's `the bullets` now misses outright instead of matching four, and recovers the same way. The detail's DOM text carries double spaces the harvest collapses, which is why `replaceText`'s spanning check now normalises whitespace. On 2026-10-16 takeaway detail 2 became "Imperative JavaScript now, declarative HTML forms in the future.", so turn 1's whole-line `find` quotes that (it still spans the styled and plain runs), and detail 3 gained "plus a growing list of agent clients. We'll try two shortly!" after "Edge", and the "Already in use" takeaway went, leaving three. Neither moves node `.5`.
meta.guards: two things, either alone reintroduces the bug. (1) `setText` in `chat/edit/apply.js`: writing only to `mainTextValue(el)`'s run and leaving the rest as authored, instead of blanking every other run in the same `pushAll` group — revert that and the `takeaway detail 2: my friends call...` slide assertion below fails because the italic, underlined words survive. (2) The whole-node rewrite for a `find` that quotes a node entire (`whole` in `replaceText`, `result.whole` in edit_text): turn 1 used to need two replies, the refusal naming `target: "{at}.5" and no find` and then the model taking it; since 2026-10-20 the first call rewrites the detail outright. Revert either half and turn 1 is refused and leaves the slide unchanged. `whole-styled-heading-by-find.json` is the recorded failure that motivated it.
